title: Stuffed Mushrooms
subtitle: Large mushrooms filled with cheese, breadcrumbs, and herbs
excerpt: Large flat mushrooms filled with a mixture of breadcrumbs, garlic, Parmesan, and parsley, then baked until the mushrooms are tender and the topping is golden and crisp. A simple starter or side dish.

recipe.sourceNotes: Stuffed mushrooms have been a British dinner party starter since the 1970s, when large flat field mushrooms or portobello mushrooms became widely available in supermarkets. The filling is effectively a gratin mixture: breadcrumbs, cheese, garlic, and herbs bound with butter or oil. Many variations exist, including additions of cream cheese, sun-dried tomatoes, or cooked sausage. The basic method remains the same: fill, top with more cheese, and bake until golden.

content.text: Remove the mushroom stalks and chop them finely to add to the stuffing: this prevents waste and adds flavour. Place the caps gill-side up on the tray. The filling should be pressed in firmly so it stays in place during baking. Drizzle a little olive oil over the top before baking to help the crumbs colour.
Heat the oven to 200 C / fan 180 C / gas 6. Finely chop the mushroom stalks. Mix with the breadcrumbs, Parmesan, garlic, parsley, lemon zest, 2 tablespoons of olive oil, salt, and pepper.
Place the mushroom caps gill-side up on a lined baking tray. Drizzle with the remaining olive oil. Press the stuffing mixture firmly into each cap.
Bake for 18 to 20 minutes until the mushrooms are tender and the topping is golden. Serve immediately.
